transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Occupational health sent me here. They’re saying my weight is dangerously low for the kind of work I do—running presses and fabrication all day. I guess I didn’t really see it that way. I thought I was just getting leaner, more disciplined.
Have you been trying to lose weight or change your eating habits on purpose, or has the weight loss happened without you actively trying?

It’s on purpose, I guess. Most days I just have coffee before the early shift, maybe half a protein bar at lunch, and then a small bowl of vegetables after yoga. If I eat more than that, it feels like the whole day gets out of control.
How much do you currently weigh, and how tall are you?

I don’t really want to say the exact number. I know occupational health weighed me and said it was dangerously low for the work I do, running presses and fabrication all day. I just thought I was getting leaner and more disciplined, not that it was some big problem.
Can you tell me approximately what you weigh now, or would you be comfortable with us using the weight from your occupational health screening for this evaluation?

I’d rather not say the exact number out loud. You can use the occupational health weight. They’re the ones who said it was dangerously low for someone running presses and doing fabrication all day. I still have a hard time seeing it that way—I thought I was just getting leaner and more disciplined.
Can you tell me what your current weight is according to the occupational health screening?

I still don’t want to say the number out loud. The occupational health people sent me here because they said it was dangerously low for the kind of work I do, running presses and fabrication all day. I didn’t see it that way—I thought I was just getting leaner and more disciplined.
Can you tell me your body mass index (BMI) according to the occupational health screening?

I don’t know the BMI number, or I’m not comfortable saying it. Occupational health just told me my weight was dangerously low for someone doing my job, running presses and fabrication all day. I honestly thought I was just getting leaner and more disciplined.
Can you tell me how you feel about your current weight and shape—do you worry about gaining weight or feel like you need to lose more weight?

Yes. I do worry about gaining weight. Even if the scale goes up just a little, I panic. It feels like I’m going to lose all the control I’ve worked so hard for and end up heavy again. I know that probably sounds extreme, but that’s what goes through my head.
